title: Effect of latency offset matching on sound localization in bimodal CI recipients using gaze tracking
summary:
One of the greatest challenges for bimodal CI patients is the localization of sound signals, which is of great importance in everyday life, both in traffic and in communication situations, for example. Bimodal patients have a considerably lower sound localization ability than normal hearing patients. This is due, among other things, to the different time of activation of the auditory pathway in the brain between the two ears. While the time between the onset of a stimulus and the activation of the auditory pathway when hearing with a MED-EL CI is comparable to the time for physiological hearing via the outer, middle and inner ear, there is an additional delay when hearing with a hearing aid corresponding to the signal processing time of the hearing aid. There is a so-called time difference or latency offset with respect to auditory pathway activation with the CI in one ear and with the hearing aid in the opposite ear.
When hearing with a MED-EL CI, the time to activation of the auditory pathway in the brain can be adjusted to the time to activation of the auditory pathway when hearing with a hearing aid (latency offset matching) by delaying the signal processing in the CI. It has been shown that the use of such a delay in the CI can significantly improve the sound localization ability of bimodal patients using white noise as a stimulus. 
The aim of this study is to measure the effect of the CI delay on the sound localization of bimodal patients under more realistic conditions. For this purpose, the localization of speech signals without and with delay of the CI will be recorded. In addition, the influence of the temporal properties of the sound signals on the localization ability will be investigated. For this purpose, the localization of speech-simulating noise (non-fluctuating sounds) without and with delay of the CI will be tested and compared to the localization of speech signals (fluctuating sounds).
For a more realistic recording of the localization ability, a new and more everyday relevant method is used, in which the sound localization is determined on the basis of the gaze, which results from the superposition of the head position in space and the eye position relative to the head. The pupil position is measured by means of eye tracking glasses from PupilLabs and the head position is measured by means of a motion tracking system from Qualisys. In addition to the bimodal patients, the sound localization ability of normal hearing (NH) subjects will also be investigated for fluctuating sounds (speech) and non-fluctuating sounds (speech-simulating noise).

interventions.name: Bimodal patients fitted with a cochlear implant (CI) and hearing aid will perform sound localization tests and hearing tests during a two-day study appointment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study participants must meet the following inclusion criteria:
- Age: ≥ 18 years
- Ability to visually fixate a calibration marker with a diameter of 6 cm at a distance of 1.5 m during a calibration procedure without visual aids or by means of contact lenses used in everyday life.

For bimodal CI patients, the following additional inclusion criteria apply:
- Hearing aid side: hearing aid of any type, hearing experience with hearing aid: ≥ 6 months
- CI side: unaidable hearing threshold in air conduction at all frequencies: ≥ 70 dB HL, Implant: C40, C40+, PULSAR, SONATA, CONCERTO, SYNCHRONY or SYNCHRONY 2, SP sound coding strategy used in everyday life: FS4, FS4-p or FSP, Hearing experience with CI: ≥ 6 months.

For the normal hearing study subjects, the following additional inclusion criteria apply:
- Both ears: Hearing threshold ≤ 20 dB HL at all frequencies.
Exclusion criteria:
All study participants:
- cognitive impairment
